pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p1.text1: A captain who does not know where he is soon knows where the rocks are. Keep your chart and mark it well.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.list1_: Use it, or press **M** with it in hand, to open the map.
Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Right-click to place a named marker; click one to change it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text1: Your {item:pirates_n_ships:chart}**chart** draws itself as you sail, inking in the coasts, shallows and open sea of the overworld around you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text1: Set {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**map tiles** side by side on a wall or table, all facing one way, to make a board.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text1: **1.** Use a tile with your chart in hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text2: **2.** Drag the frame over the waters you want and pick a zoom.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text4: Each tile costs an ink sac; one {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink** pays for eight. Anyone who has charted more can press **Update** to fill in the blanks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.list1_: **Two points off the starboard bow:** a little right of ahead.
**On the beam:** square off the side.
**Abaft the beam:** behind it, toward the stern.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text1: The lookout calls points of the compass from the bow, 32 to the circle:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text1: Pirate fences sell blank {item:pirates_n_ships:treasure_map}**treasure maps**, and wrecks hold some. Use one and it marks the nearest unfound treasure.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text2: Hold it to see the red X and the way there. At the X, dig into the sand for the chest.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text3: Pirate islands hide their chests under the sand: beneath two crossed logs, by a cairn, or among the ribs of an old boat.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p7.text1: The ocean floor is strewn with wrecks, each with a chest of ship's stores: doubloons, rum, supplies, now and then a treasure map. Tall wrecks lie in deep water. Bring something to breathe and see down there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.title: Charts and navigation
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p1.text1: Sooner or later someone will want your ship, your cargo or your head. Learn the blade, the pistol and the great guns before you need them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text2: **2.** **Aim:** sneak and use it with an empty hand. The upper half raises the barrel, the lower half lowers it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text3: **3.** **Fire:** use it with an empty hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text1: The barrel needs five seconds to cool. A ball smashes the wood it strikes, and a hole below the waterline lets the sea in. Hit square; a grazing ball glances off.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text1: Both load like a ball, after the powder. {item:pirates_n_ships:chain_shot}**Chain shot** breaks no hull but tears sails, cuts ropes and breaks ratlines. Torn cloth mends slowly by itself.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text2: {item:pirates_n_ships:grapeshot}**Grapeshot** bursts into a cone of pellets that hurt men and break nothing. Sweep a crowded deck before you board.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** mounts on a fence, a wall, bars or any full block. Load it like a cannon, then hold right click with an empty hand: it follows your eye and fires when you let go.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text1: Post a hand at a gun with the whistle and stock powder and shot in a chest, barrel or crate within 4 blocks on the same ship. Blow **Load!**, then **Fire!**: every manned, loaded gun fires, and the crew reloads it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text2: **Fire at will** lets the crews pick targets; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:grappling_hook}**grappling hook** bites into ships and land. Right click to throw it, with 32 blocks of rope. Or hold it in your off hand, load it into a musket and fire it, with 64 blocks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.list1: **Two ships:** hooked from your own ship, the rope hauls them side by side.
**Haul:** hold sneak with the rope in hand and walk back.
**Climb:** right-click your own rope when the hook is two blocks or more above you.
**Make fast:** use a cleat or mooring ring of yours while the hook is out.
**Let go:** sneak and use with an empty hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text1: It slips off water, leaves, glass panes and creatures.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text1: Use a rope made fast to a cleat or ring to slide down it, from your masthead onto her deck.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text2: With the ships alongside, use a {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** on top of your gunwale. Keep the ships together or it breaks. Hold the plank and look at your rail: the board it would lay shows in green, and a red cell marks what stands in the way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text3: String a {item:pirates_n_ships:ratline_net}**ratline net** between two {item:pirates_n_ships:chainplate}**chainplates** on top of one run of railing and it hangs along the rail as a boarding net. Boarders coming over the rail are held a moment; your own crew pass. Three cutlass blows cut one down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.list1: An empty hand takes a sword from your chests.
Her deck clear: "Her deck is yours", and they come home.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text1: With a gangway across or her rail two blocks off at most, blow **Board!**. Your hands cross and fight her crew; gunners and helmsman stay.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text2: Pirates alongside board you the same way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p19.list1: Take goods from her hold while aboard: plundered.
Sink her with the last shot: the deed is yours.
Kill every fighter and hold her deck: she is yours, crew and all.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p19.text1: Merchantmen, navy patrols and pirates sail the sea lanes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p19.text2: Taking a merchant is piracy. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:cutlass}**cutlass** is heavy and wide, made for the slash.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p20.list1: **Pirates** attack you and the navy on sight.
**Navy soldiers** shoot at you only when you are wanted.
**Navy officers** are deadly with the saber.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p20.text1: Striking navy men is a crime; killing pirates is not.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p21.text1: Every pirate island has a captain with a bounty of 300 doubloons. Sneak and use him with a sword in hand to call a duel; his crew keeps out of it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p21.text2: Slain, he drops his hat, a treasure map and your bounty proof.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p22.text1: Linger at a navy outpost or seafarer village and pirates may raid it. Kill every raider to beat them off.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p23.text1: Hats and coats are armour too; a hat gives one point. The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_hat}**captain's hat** you only win from a pirate captain. The {item:pirates_n_ships:pirate_hat}**pirate hat**:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p25.text1: In navy blue and white: the {item:pirates_n_ships:officer_hat}**officer's bicorne** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_coat}**officer's coat**, three points.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p26.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_breeches}**officer's breeches**, two points, and {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_boots}**boots**, one.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p27.text1: In charcoal and gold: the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_coat}**captain's coat** and {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_breeches}**breeches**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p29.text1: The **kraken** rises beside ships in the deep ocean, most often at night and in storms. It drags hulls down and smashes masts. Strike its eyes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p29.text2: It leaves a {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**kraken beak** and {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:rapier}**rapier** is light and long, made for the thrust.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text2: The {item:pirates_n_ships:saber}**saber** is the officer's blade, good at both.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p30.text1: Sharks hunt swimmers, and blood drives them into a frenzy. Stay on deck or in a boat and they leave you alone.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p31.text1: In a storm at sea a **waterspout** pulls in and lifts what comes near, and tears set sails. Steer clear, or furl first.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p31.text2: In the deep ocean a **whirlpool** drags boats and swimmers under and turns ships about.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.list1_: **Slash:** a quick left click. A wide, short arc.
**Thrust:** hold left click a moment, then release. Narrow, longer and harder, but slow to recover if it misses.
**Guard:** hold right click. It stops every blow from the front, at a cost in stamina. Blows from behind or the side get through.
**Parry:** tap right click just before a blow lands. The attacker staggers and you may **riposte** for extra harm.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text1: While you hold a sword, right click belongs to the blade. Put it away to open a door or take the helm.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text1: A brass-framed bar shows your stamina. Attacks, guarding and missed parries drain it; rest refills it. Empty, you can neither guard nor parry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text2: Pirates fight as you do. Parry when the arm goes up or back, but beware the feint that baits an early parry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pistol}**pistol** is a single-shot flintlock. Its ball scatters.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:musket}**musket** hits harder and flies flatter and truer. Both fire {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**lead shot** with gunpowder.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text1: **1.** **Load:** with shot and powder in your pack, hold right click: three seconds for the pistol, five for the musket.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text2: **2.** **Aim:** hold right click. After a second of steady aim the shot tightens.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text3: **3.** **Fire:** left click. From the hip the ball scatters wide.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text4: Letting go of right click never fires. Sneak to lower an aimed gun.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text5: In the rain a quarter of your shots misfire; the charge stays in.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text1: Click the deck where the **front** of the carriage should stand, by the rail: the barrel overhangs one block ahead. Both halves need a block beneath them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text2: A cannon cannot turn sideways. Lay your ship so her broadside bears.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.title: Weapons and combat
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.heading: Crew
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text1: One captain cannot work the winch, the helm, the pumps and the guns at once. A crew can.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text2: Hire hands, feed, pay and bunk them, and they sail her for you. The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** gives the orders.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.heading: Desertion
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text1: A hand below 20 morale for two dawns means to desert: he tells you, then walks off at the next port. Lift his spirits above 20 and he stays.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text2: On some seas a miserable crew rises in mutiny and takes the ship. Your server tells you whether yours is one.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.heading: Fire at will
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_1: Navy flag: the Jolly Roger, and ships found out under false colours.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_2: Jolly Roger: navy ships, merchants and unflagged ships.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_3: Merchant flag or none: only the Jolly Roger.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text1: On **Fire at will** your gun crews fire at the nearest hostile ship within 64 blocks. Your flag decides who is hostile:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text2: Turn her to bring the guns to bear; see [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.heading: Hiring hands
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_1: **Sailors**, at seafarer villages: 10 doubloons. Not for a captain the villagers refuse to trade with.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_2: **Navy ratings**, at navy outposts: 15. Enlisted officers only.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_3: **Pirates**, at pirate islands: 20. Only for a friend of the pirates, or a Buccaneer or worse.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text1: The **Crew** tab of a harbour master's desk lists who seeks a berth. Each asks a fee, then a daily wage.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text2: Bring your ship within about 32 blocks of the port first: the new hand walks straight aboard.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text3: Every hand needs a free {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock**. The desk refuses a hand you cannot bunk.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.heading: Stations
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.show_me1: Show me: hands at the rail
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text1: A station is a block a hand can work: the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch**, the **helm**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text2: A posted hand walks to his station, even under way, and stays there while she sails.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text3: A hand with nothing to do strolls the deck, or leans on the {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}**railing** a while and watches the sea. Any order calls him off.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.heading: The captain's whistle
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_1: Use it on a hand, then on a station: he takes that station.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_2: Use it on a hand at a station: he is released.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_3: Sneak and use it on a hand: he is dismissed. Only you, or whoever hired him, may do so.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_4: Use it in the air: the order wheel opens. Click an order, or hold the use key, aim and let go.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text1: The wheel: **Hoist**, **Reef** and **Furl sails**, **Man the pumps**, **Fire!**, **Load!**, **Fire at will**, the anchor, **Release crew**. The anchor is one order that switches: **Drop anchor** while it is stowed or coming up, **Raise anchor** while it is out.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text2: The ship screen at the helm gives the same orders. See [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.heading: Orders, not assignments
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text1: Blow an order and free hands on deck man the nearest unmanned stations that can carry it out. A hand you posted yourself is never moved.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text2: If nobody can, you are told why.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text3: **Release crew** sends everyone off and ends **Fire at will**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.heading: A helmsman
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text1: A hand at the helm steers the course he is given, but leaves the sails alone: order **Hoist sails** as well. Take the wheel and he lets go.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.heading: Hammocks
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text1: Hang a hammock between two supports at the same height, such as posts, walls or the hull side: click the block next to one while looking toward the other.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text2: At nightfall every hand off station turns in to the nearest free hammock. A night in one cheers him; a night aboard without one does not.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.heading: Your own bunk
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text1: Right-click a free hammock at night to sleep in it as in a bed, even under way. Your respawn point sails with the ship.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot** is the captain's bed for the great cabin, and works the same way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.heading: Morale and wages
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_1: A night in a hammock: up. Without one: down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_3: Hungry or thirsty: down every day, and slower at work.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_4: Rum: up. Scurvy: down every day.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text1: Every hand has a morale from 0 to 100; use the whistle on him to read it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text2: Every dawn each hand eats from the [[pirates_n_ships:provisions|Provisions]] and wants 2 doubloons, paid from the chests and crates aboard, then from your purse.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.title: Crew
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p1.te: Every captain starts with planks, a helm and more courage than sense. Follow these steps.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.te: Build a wooden hull floating in the water.
Leave a one-block gap to the shore and every other build. Whatever touches the hull becomes part of the ship.
Natural ground (dirt, sand, raw stone, leaves) stays behind; cut and crafted blocks sail with her.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p3.te: Place a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** on deck. The bow is where the helmsman looks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p4.te: Raise a mast of logs or fences with two rows of {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards** across it, 2 to 8 blocks apart.
Add a {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** on deck, and a {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** for an anchor.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p5.te: Use the helm: everything joined to it becomes one ship. Use the winch to set sail: furled, half, full.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p6.te: Hold right-click on the helm and turn with the mouse or A and D.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p7.te: Use the capstan to drop or weigh anchor.
To unmake her, sneak and use the helm with an empty hand and press **Disassemble** twice.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p8.te: A seafarer village's shipwright builds sloops to order: see the **Orders** tab of the harbour master's desk, and [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.title: Your first ship
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.heading: Flags
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.text1: A flag tells every ship on the horizon who you are, and the sea holds you to it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.heading: The colours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_1: {item:pirates_n_ships:merchant_flag}**Merchant flag**, or none: neutral to all.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_flag}**Navy flag**: navy and merchants are friends, pirates foes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_3: **Any banner:** your own flag, neutral to all.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.heading: The Jolly Roger
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text1: Under the {item:pirates_n_ships:jolly_roger_flag}**Jolly Roger** the pirates let you be and merchants may strike to you. The navy fires on everyone aboard on sight, and being seen under it is a crime.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.heading: The flagpole
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_1: **Use it with a flag:** the flag flies after three seconds; you get the old one back.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_2: **Empty hand:** strike the colours, or raise them again.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_3: **Sneak, empty hand:** take the flag down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**flagpole** flies the flag downwind from its top, a block high and a block and a half long, so leave it room.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.heading: Tall poles
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text1: Stack flagpoles into one pole up to 6 blocks tall. The top flies the flag, and you may work it from any block.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flag_pedestal}**flag pedestal** is a sturdy foot: set it on solid ground and stand a pole in it. Breaking it brings the whole pole down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.heading: False colours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text1: A ship flies the highest flag on her poles. Under the navy flag you pass the navy while your record is clean, but a suspect may be found out by any navy soldier in sight. Then you are charged heavily and hunted for five minutes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text2: Firing on struck colours, a merchant flag or a banner is a crime, and your crew's shots are charged to you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p7.heading: Striking your colours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p7.text1: Strike your flag to surrender: navy and pirates stop attacking. Raise the Jolly Roger again and the chase is back on. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p8.heading: Dyed sails
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p8.text1: Use a dye on the upper yard of a square sail, or the head cleat of a triangular one, to colour the cloth; white dye brings back plain canvas. A large square sail takes a banner the same way. Colours are only for show.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.title: Flags
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p1.tex: Every block and item a hand may need, a line on each, and the chapter that tells the rest.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p2.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**Helm:** launches, steers and takes apart a ship. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**Ship's bell:** rings when struck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**Bilge pump:** pumps a flooded hold. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**Hull patch:** closes a breach.
{item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**Flagpole:** flies your colours. [[pirates_n_ships:flags|Flags]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:flag_pedestal}**Flag pedestal:** a carved plinth a flagpole stands in.
{item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**Name Board:** shows her name across the boards it joins.

{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_eagle}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_skull}**Figureheads:** a mermaid, lion, eagle or skull for the bow.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**Ship's lantern:** a lantern that burns under water.
{item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern window:** shuttered windows for the great cabin.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coil:** coiled rope for the deck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**Yard:** a spar; two on a mast make a square sail. [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**Chart table:** a captain's table.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**Sea cot:** the captain's bed at sea.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**Hammock:** a bunk for one hand. [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**Boarding plank:** a bridge to an enemy deck.

{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_port}**Railing, railing port:** a rail along a block's edge; click again to rail another. A cannon fires and a boarding plank goes out through the port.

{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_bulwark}{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_bulwark_port}**Bulwark, bulwark gun port:** a solid plank wall along a block's edge, placed like a railing. A cannon behind it fires into it; through the gun port it fires at every elevation, and the port's lid opens for the gun or by hand.

{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_gate}**Railing gate:** a railing section that swings open like a fence gate (use it, or redstone), so crew and boarding planks pass when it is open; a lantern hangs below or stands on any railing post, and a chain runs on from it.
{item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**Cleat:** holds a stay, a rope line or a grappling rope.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**Rope:** rigs stays and rope lines.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**Sail winch:** works every sail aboard. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**Capstan:** drops and weighs the anchor. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring ring:** catches and holds a grappling hook.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines:** rope nets for climbing aloft.
{item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**Crow's nest:** the lookout's barrel. A station.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p3.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_crate}**Cargo crate:** 32 stacks of one item. [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**Hardtack,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**salted fish,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork:** food that never spoils.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**Rum:** cheers a crew and warms a swimmer.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p4.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**Lead shot:** a ball for pistol or musket.
{item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**Swivel gun:** a small gun on a yoke. A station.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p5.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**Bounty proof:** proof of a kill; hand it to a navy officer.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**Ship commission:** an armed sloop earned by rank.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p6.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**Map tile:** a board for a drawn chart.

{item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**Shipwright's toolkit,** from the {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer,** {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw** and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails:** joins a broken ship.
{item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**Kraken beak,** {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink:** spoils of the deep.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p7.tex: All of them, with spawn eggs for the folk and beasts of the sea, are in the "Pirates 'n' Ships" creative tab.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.title: The ship's inventory
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.heading: Law
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.text1: The Crown keeps a ledger on every soul at sea. Stay honest and the navy is your friend; turn pirate and you had better be fast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.heading: The three powers
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_1: Killing pirates pleases the navy; plunder pleases the pirates; trade pleases the villagers.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_2: Good standing means better prices. Villagers stop trading at −60.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_3: Liked pirates leave you be until you strike first. At −60 the navy fires on sight.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text1: The navy, the pirates and the villagers each remember you, from −100 to 100.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.heading: Navy patrols
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text1: Navy patrols chase the Jolly Roger, false colours they see through, and wanted men.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text2: Strike your colours and their guns fall silent. Outrun them and they give up.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.heading: Careers
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_1: **The navy:** enlist with an officer once the navy trusts you, and rise from Midshipman to Admiral.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_2: **Infamy:** plunder and taken ships make you a Buccaneer, a Dread Captain and a Pirate Lord.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_3: **Letter of marque:** bought from a navy officer; pirates you kill earn prize money.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.text1: You may climb only one ladder.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.heading: Rewards of rank
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_1: **Lieutenant:** the navy flag, free docking at navy outposts, and an officer's uniform and saber.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_2: **Navy Captain:** a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**ship commission** for an armed sloop, and cheaper ships at navy desks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_3: **Dread Captain:** a pirate sloop from a pirate island's fence.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.text1: Your title rides before your name in chat and over your head.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.heading: Your record
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text1: Every crime adds to your record: theft, violence, plunder aboard, false colours and, worst of all, piracy and desertion.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text2: From 10 you are a **suspect**, from 50 **wanted**, from 200 **notorious**. Keep clean and it fades day by day.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text3: Theft counts only when someone sees it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.heading: Fines and bounties
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text1: Right-click a navy officer with doubloons to pay off your record. He will not deal with a wanted man, and no coin buys a pardon for the notorious.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text2: A wanted man carries a bounty. Kill him and bring the {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**bounty proof** to a navy officer; alive pays more.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.heading: The notice board
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:notice_board}**notice board** lists every bounty, and places your own.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.heading: Shackles
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:shackles}**Shackles** take a beaten foe alive: use them on a creature at a quarter of its health or less. Bosses cannot be taken.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.heading: Prisoners
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_1: A prisoner stops fighting and never wanders off.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_2: Use the shackles on it again to lead it, or to let go.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_3: Left alone outside a cell, it tries to slip away.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.text1: Right-click a navy officer with an empty hand, prisoners close by, to turn them in or ransom them. Your shackles come back.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.heading: Press-ganging
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text1: Right-click a shackled sailor on your own ship with the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** to press-gang him into your crew. He comes aboard sullen, and it is a crime.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text2: Sneak-use your own prisoner with an empty hand to set him free.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.heading: The brig
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_door}**brig door** locks and unlocks with a {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_key}**brig key**. Locked, it opens only for whoever placed it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.heading: Bars and keys
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_bars}**Brig bars** connect like iron bars. A prisoner shut in a small space by blocks, bars and a locked brig door is **in a cell** and stays put.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text2: Any brig key opens any brig door. Keep keys away from your prisoners.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.title: Law
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p1.text1: These pages are for the keeper of a server, not the hand at the wheel: the settings a keeper reaches for first, and the orders an operator may give.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text1: Open them under Mods, then Pirates 'n' Ships, then Config (on Fabric with Mod Menu). Gameplay sits in the server config, which every client receives; looks and sounds sit in each player's client config.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text2: Every feature has a switch and every strength a value. Below: section.name, default after the colon.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p3.list1_: assembly.max\_blocks: 2048. The largest ship a helm launches.
ship\_screen.enabled: true. Off, sneak-using the helm takes the ship apart at once.
helm.wheel.drag\_steering: true. Off, the wheel is clicked in thirds.
dry\_hull.flood\_breath: true. Off, flood water inside a hull never drowns.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p4.list1_: melee.skill\_based\_combat: true. Off, our swords fight like vanilla swords.
firearms.fire\_on\_attack: true. Off, guns fire when right click is released.
combat.cannon\_block\_damage: true. Cannon fire also obeys mobGriefing and spawn protection.
almanac.give\_on\_first\_join: true. One Almanac for every new hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p5.list1_: /pirates career: your rank, standing and letter of marque.
/pirates rep: your standing with the navy, the pirates and the villagers.
/pirates waves: the sea state where you stand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p6.list1_: /pirates law score, fine, bounty list, clear.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p7.text1: Ship templates, trade goods and weapon timings are data files, and tags decide what never sails, what keeps water out and which foods keep or cure scurvy. A datapack can replace any of them, or add to the Almanac itself.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.title: The Quartermaster's ledger
pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p1.text1: An honest chart leaves blank what nobody has sailed. These waters the Almanac cannot describe yet, because nobody has built them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.list1: **A ship's logbook** to record your voyages and deeds.
**Paint for the hull,** to dye her planks your own colours.
**A wanted poster** of your own, beyond the chat, the notice board and the rank box.
**Feints of your own** with the sword, and a choice of side for your cut and parry.
**Sounds of their own** for most of the work aboard.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.text1: If these pages and the sea disagree, the mistake is the Almanac's. Tell whoever keeps your server.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.title: Not yet charted
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p1.te: An empty pantry sinks more ships than cannon ever did. Every dawn your crew takes a day's food and water from the stores aboard.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p2.te: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pantry}**pantry** is the ship's food store, opening like a chest. Anything edible counts; a hand eats about a loaf of bread a day.
Sneak and use it empty-handed to read what it holds. A hopper below takes out only the waste.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p3.te: Fresh food spoils after five days in the pantry.
Preserved food never spoils: bread, dried kelp, honey and the sailor's own {item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**hardtack**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p4.te: {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**Salted fish** and {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork** keep as long as you sail.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p5.te: A {item:pirates_n_ships:water_barrel}**water barrel** holds 16 rations, and each hand drinks one a day. It comes off the bench full.
Buckets and bottles fill or empty it, and rain tops it up.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p6.te: Hungry hands work at three quarters pace, thirsty ones at half. Three days without food, or one without water, and the whole crew deserts.
After eight days without fresh food comes scurvy. Fresh food cures it, fruit best.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p7.te: While there is {item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**rum** aboard, each hand gets a daily ration and cheers up. Stow ten days' worth or more and they drink double and work slowly.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p8.te: Swimming in cold or frozen seas soon freezes you. A boat, a deck, leather armour or a swig of rum keeps you warm.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p9.te: Prisoners in your brig eat and drink half a hand's share, and get no rum. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.title: Provisions
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p1.text1: Learn the wind, learn your canvas, and keep the bow where you want it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.head: Oars
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.text: In a calm or against the wind, whistle **Row**: every hand not at a station takes an {item:pirates_n_ships:oar}**oar** at the rail, the sides in turn, and pulls her along at up to 3 blocks a second. A hand seated on an **oar bench** pulls a quarter harder.
The same entry then reads **Ship oars**. Any other order ends the rowing too, and the hands ship oars themselves once the sails are faster.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.head: Mooring
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.text: A moored ship is simply a ship lying still at her berth: bring her in slowly and drop the anchor.

{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring rings** and cleats serve the grappling hook. A hook catches on a ring and holds longer there; use a ring or cleat on your own ship to make a hooked ship fast. See [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.head: The gangway
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** bridges your deck and the quay. Use it on the edge of either, toward the other: it lies as one straight board, up or down to a high pier, up to six blocks.
It goes where the ship goes, but let her drift along the quay and it breaks. Sneak and use it with an empty hand to stow it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.head: Waves and weather
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.text: Fair weather brings a low swell, rain rough seas, a thunderstorm high crests. A small boat rides them far more than a big one.
In rough seas every open hatch or low rim near the waterline takes water. Close your hatches and man a pump before a storm.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.head: Ratlines
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.list: Click the side of a mast to hang a net like a ladder.
Click the deck or the gunwale to lay a sloped net, rising the way you face.
Click a ratline to add the next one to its run. Sneak to place against the clicked side.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.text: {item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines** are rope nets for climbing aloft.
A net needs something to rest on: break one and those hanging from it fall too.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.head: Ratline nets
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.text: A {item:pirates_n_ships:ratline_net}**ratline net** runs from a {item:pirates_n_ships:chainplate}**chainplate** on the rail to a {item:pirates_n_ships:mast_hoop}**mast hoop** up the mast. Use the net on one, then on the other; the line between them must be clear.
Walk into the net and hold forward or jump to climb; sneak to hold on. String several chainplates to one hoop and the space between them is netted too.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p16.head: Chainplate and hoop
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p16.text: Break a net, its chainplate or put a block into it and that net comes down. Break the hoop and they all do.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p17.head: The ship's bell
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p17.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**ship's bell** sits on a post or a wall. Right-click it and it rings. It does not call your crew, but in a harbour every bell rings the alarm when raiders come.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.head: The crow's nest
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest** is a barrel for the masthead, set on a log, fence, wall or any solid top. Climb in over the rim; sneak to stay put.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.head: The lookout
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.list: **Ships,** by their flag: merchant, navy, pirate, wreck or just a sail.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.text: Whoever stands in the nest keeps the lookout, you or a hand you post with the whistle. The lookout calls what is new to everyone aboard:
Each call rings a small bell and lights a diamond on your compass: white for land, red for a pirate, blue for the navy.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text1: One wind blows for every soul at sea. It veers and freshens slowly through the day; rain and thunder stiffen it. Read it from the white streaks on the water, from flags and from bellying sails.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text2: Aboard, a pale arrow on your compass rose shows where the wind comes from. The longer the arrow, the stronger the wind; it glows amber in a gust.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p20.head: The ship's panels
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p20.list: **The compass,** bottom left: heading, wind, speed in knots and rudder angle.
**The hull strip,** bottom right: one cell per compartment, filling blue as water comes in, with a red mark at a breach.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p20.text: While you are aboard, two panels watch over her:
Her name, load and crew are on the ship screen at the helm; see [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text1: A square sail hangs between two {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards**, rows of yard blocks laid across the ship. The middle block marks the mast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text2: Both yards stand one block forward of the mast, in the column in front of it, never in the mast's own column. So the cloth hangs before the mast, as on any ship at sea.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text3: **1.** Set the upper yard across the ship, its middle block just forward of the mast.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text4: **2.** Set a second yard the same way, 2 to 8 blocks straight below it, with only air or mast between their middles.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text5: **3.** The pair is now one sail. You place no canvas: the cloth is drawn between them.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text1: A square sail loves a wind from astern and is useless close to the wind. Longer yards set further apart make a bigger sail, and three yards on one mast make two sails.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text2: Click a yard that heads no sail and it tells you what is wrong with the rig.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text1: A triangular sail is rigged with {item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**rope** and three {item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**cleats**. It is the sail for a wind on the beam.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text2: **1.** Put one cleat high on the side of the mast: the head.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text3: **2.** Put one further forward and lower, on the deck or a bowsprit: the tack.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text4: **3.** Put one straight below the head: the clew.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text5: **4.** Use a rope on the head cleat, then on the tack cleat. A stay runs between them and the cloth fills the triangle.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text6: A rope between two cleats or mooring rings that is no stay becomes a sagging rope line, for a rail or rigging.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text1: Every sail has three trims: furled, half and full. Use the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** on deck to work every sail at once, or click an upper yard or a head cleat with an empty hand to work that sail alone.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text2: No sail drives straight into the wind. A sail that shakes and hangs slack is in the no-go zone: bear away. Your crew braces the yards for you.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.show_: Show me: steering at the helm
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text1: Hold right-click on the {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** to take the wheel, then move the mouse or hold A and D to turn: right or D to starboard, left or A to port. Let go and the wheel stays put.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text2: The line above your hotbar shows the rudder angle. The rudder bites only while she moves through the water, and works the other way round when she goes astern.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text1: Wind on the sails heels her over and the hull rights itself; near her limit the sails spill their wind. A wide, shallow hull stands stiffest.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text2: She is ballasted as you built her. What you load later can make her list: trim the cargo and pump her dry, as [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]] explains.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.show_: Show me: dropping and weighing anchor
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** works the anchor, which hangs outside the hull on its side. Use it to let go, and again to weigh.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text2: Once the anchor bites, she swings to lie head to her chain. Over water too deep for the chain, the capstan refuses to let go.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text3: A ship pulling harder than her anchor holds drags it. Furl before you anchor.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.title: Sailing
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.heading: Ships
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.text1: Timber that agreed to float. Mend her quickly when she is hurt.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p10.text1: The toolkit needs a {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer** and a {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text1: Add leather, and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails**: each repair takes 4.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text1: **1.** Sneak and use the toolkit on the part you keep. Green sparkles show where pieces meet.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text2: **2.** Bring the broken piece against her, straight and face to face. Bridge a one-block gap with planks.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text3: **3.** Use the toolkit on the broken piece, and she is whole.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text4: Only pieces of the same ship join, of up to 200 blocks each.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p13.show_m: Show me: her name and figurehead
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p13.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**name board** (any sign and a gold nugget make three) fixed on her side shows her name once she is launched and named; boards side by side join, and the name grows across the row.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p14.text1: A figurehead hangs on the bow block you click and looks toward you. The {item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}**mermaid** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}**lion**:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text1: An {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}**oak railing** runs along a block's edge; click again to rail another edge.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_port}**railing port** is the gap in it: cannons fire through it, boarders cross there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text3: A {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_gate}**railing gate** swings open like a fence gate, and a lantern hangs from any railing post.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text4: A {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_bulwark}**bulwark** is a solid wall instead: a gun behind it fires into it, so cut a {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_bulwark_port}**gun port**, whose lid opens for the gun.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p17.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**ship's lantern** hangs or stands, and burns even under water.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p17.text2: {item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coils** stack four to a spot.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p18.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern windows** go into a wall from outside; right-click to work the shutters.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p18.text2: The {item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**chart table** is a captain's table with a chart spread on it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p19.text1: Sleep in a {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot** aboard and you respawn at it wherever she has gone.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.heading: Launching at the helm
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_1: Air, water and natural ground never join; logs and planks do.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_2: Up to 2048 blocks. A dock touching the hull counts, so keep a gap.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text1: Use a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** to launch her: every block joined to it becomes part of her.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text2: A **name tag** on her helm renames her.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text1: Seafarer villages build ships to order. The **Orders** tab of the harbour master's desk shows each ship's price, days and materials.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text2: **1.** Bring the doubloons and materials and press **Order** for a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_receipt}**ship receipt** that counts the days.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text3: **2.** When it reads "Ready for pickup", use the desk with the receipt in hand.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text4: **3.** She waits at a berth by the pier.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text5: Armed sloops are never for sale: earn one by rank or take one at sea ([[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]], [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]]).
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p21.list1_: Keep near the middle of the world: very far out, ships stop moving true.
A ship floats only on water beneath her own hull.
Cargo and flood water make her list and sit lower.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.heading: The ship screen
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_1: **Ship:** her name, hull, load, sails, crew, supplies and **Disassemble**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_2: **Crew:** orders, and every hand's morale, station and pay.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_3: **Stations:** who works where; **Man** sends a free hand to one.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.text1: Sneak and use your helm with an empty hand. Only the owner may open it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.heading: Taking her apart
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text1: Press **Disassemble** twice and she becomes blocks. Not while she moves, heels over 6°, or something solid is in the way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text2: A ship whose helm is broken cannot be steered or taken apart until you place a new helm on her deck.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.heading: The dry hold
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_2: **Leaky:** fences, walls, bars, panes, ladders, chains.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_3: **Doors, trapdoors, fence gates:** watertight only when shut.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text1: Rooms below the lowest place water could pour in stay dry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text2: Dry volume keeps her up; flood water drags her down.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.heading: Flooding
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text1: A hull block destroyed below the waterline is a breach, and an open door or hatch there lets the sea in too.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text2: Rooms joined by an open door fill together. Any block placed in the breach stops the flow.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text3: Under the flood water you hold your breath, as in the sea.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.heading: Pumps
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text1: Place a {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump** on the hold floor or the deck above it, and hold right-click to drain the highest flooded room below.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text2: Pumping is hungry work: order a hand to **Man the pumps**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.heading: Patching a breach
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.text1: Stand inside, look at the edge of the hole and use a {item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**hull patch**. The water stops at once.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.heading: When she breaks in two
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text1: Shoot through the only block joining two parts and she splits. The part with the helm stays your ship; the other drifts as a wreck.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**shipwright's toolkit** nails her together again.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.title: Ships
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.heading: Cargo and trade
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.text1: Buy cheap, carry it where it is wanted, and sell it dear. That is the whole of honest trade.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p10.list1_: **Goods:** buy and sell. Green goods are cheap here, orange goods wanted here.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p10.text1: Stay near the desk, or the market closes.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p11.text1: Buying raises a price and selling lowers it; prices drift back day by day. Carry a good from a port that makes it to one that wants it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p11.text2: Spices fetch the most. Tropical ports grow sugar, cocoa, {item:pirates_n_ships:tobacco}**tobacco** and {item:pirates_n_ships:spices}**spices**; colder ports deal in fish, timber and iron. {item:pirates_n_ships:cloth}**Cloth** you can weave yourself.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text1: Goods from a captured or sunk ship carry a plunder mark. Only a pirate fence buys them, cheaply and with no questions.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text2: Honest harbour masters report plunder to the navy, and a navy ship or fort that sees much of it in your hold suspects you of piracy.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p13.text1: A navy outpost charges a small fee when your ship berths or anchors there, once a day. Leave it unpaid and its desk will not trade with you. Trusted captains and officers dock free.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p14.text1: A **contract** asks you to carry goods to another port by a deadline. You pay a deposit and get it back with the reward.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p14.text2: **Quests** pay doubloons and standing: hunts, prisoners, cargo runs, treasure hunts, escorts, raids and patrols. Each desk offers a few at a time, each with a deadline.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.heading: Crates and barrels
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_barrel}**Cargo barrel:** 1536 items, whatever their stack size; best for rum.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.text1: Bulk cargo goes in containers that hold great amounts of **one kind of item**.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.heading: Stowing
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_1: Use with a stack to put it in, with an empty hand to take a stack out.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_2: Sneak-use with an empty hand to put in everything of that kind you carry.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_3: A broken container keeps its cargo, and hoppers work on it.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.text1: Items that do not stack are refused, and stolen and clean goods never share a container.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.heading: Weight and trim
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text1: Cargo weighs: containers grow heavier as they fill, and a chest presses down where it stands.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text2: Keep heavy cargo low, spread and amidships. A laden ship sits deeper, floods sooner and is slower to turn.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text3: The ship screen at the helm reads her load, from Light to Overloaded.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.heading: The sea chest
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_1: Use it in the air to carry it on your back: slow, no jumping or swimming.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_2: Place it on water and it floats with wind and current.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_3: Sneak-use to pick it up; strike it to knock it loose.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_chest}**sea chest** holds 54 stacks and keeps them when broken, carried or floated.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.heading: The paddle
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.text1: Use a {item:pirates_n_ships:paddle}**paddle** on a floating sea chest to sit on the lid and paddle it like a little boat. Sneak to get off.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.heading: Doubloons
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text1: The gold {item:pirates_n_ships:doubloon}**doubloon** is the coin of the sea. You earn it by trading, from pirates' purses, wrecks and buried treasure, and from bounties, contracts and quests.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text2: Keep them in your inventory; markets take them from there.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.heading: Harbours
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_1: **Seafarer villages:** a quay and a pier on a beach, then cobbled streets that bend and branch inland past cottages, taverns, a shipwright, a market and often a chapel or a beacon tower.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_2: **Navy outposts:** rarer stone forts with cannon and a garrison.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_3: **Pirate islands:** rarer still, camps under the Jolly Roger: a rough jetty, then tents, huts and a tavern along winding trails up from the beach. Strangers are not welcome.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.text1: Every port has a harbour master's desk.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.heading: The harbour master
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.text1: Right-click the harbour master or his {item:pirates_n_ships:harbor_desk}**harbour master's desk** to open the market. A desk you place inside a port joins that port.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.title: Cargo and trade
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p1.text1: So you mean to go to sea. Good. This book holds what every captain before you learned the hard way.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.list1: Use it to read; sneak and use it on any surface to lay it down.
Turn pages with the corner arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel. Escape closes it.
{#2e6a24}Green ink{/} is a tip, {#9a1c14}red ink{/} a warning, {#2a4580}blue ink{/} a link to another chapter.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.text1: Lost yours? Bind a new {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_almanac}**Captain's Almanac**:
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text1: Some pages carry a **Show me** button: the Almanac acts the thing out on a little model ship.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text2: Or hover an item, such as the cannon, and hold the Ponder key.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text1: Start with [[pirates_n_ships:first_ship|Your first ship]]: from planks to sail in a few pages.
pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text2: At the back, [[pirates_n_ships:inventory|The ship's inventory]] lists every block and item, [[pirates_n_ships:ledger|The Quartermaster's ledger]] serves a server's keeper, and [[pirates_n_ships:not_yet|Not yet charted]] owns up to what is still missing.

pirates_n_ships.configuration.wave_effec: Vanilla boats on the waves tilt along the slope of the sea by up to this many degrees (0 = no tilt; the rider stays upright)
The camera rolls with the ship while you are aboard
Ticks the camera sway takes to fade in when you board or land and out when you leave the ship (0 = instant)
Fraction of the ship's roll the camera follows (1 = the full roll)
Faint foam streaks on the water, stretched along the direction the waves run, more in a higher sea; none in a calm sea
Foam streaks tried per tick at one block of wave height above foam_min_amplitude, growing with the square root of that height (about a third of them land, on the crests)
Life of one foam streak in ticks, including fading in and out
No foam below this wave height in blocks (calm sea 0.15, moderate 0.6, rough 1.2, storm 2.0)
Horizontal distance from the camera in blocks within which foam appears
Spray and a splash at the bow when it digs into a wave in rough or stormy seas

The sea surface rises and falls with the waves (a moving water surface around you; ships, swimming and collisions still use the flat sea level). Off, and always with Sodium, Embeddium, Iris, Oculus or VulkanMod: flat water
Size in blocks of the moving surface's cells beyond surface_mid_radius (4, 8, 16, 32 or 64; other values round down)
Water depth in blocks from which the surface moves with the full wave height; shallower water moves less, one block deep not at all, so waves never cut into a beach
Distance from the camera in blocks within which the moving surface has one point every 4 blocks; beyond it the far cells reach to the render distance
Distance from the camera in blocks within which the moving surface has one point per block (rounded up to 4)
Also draw the moving surface from below, so it shows when you look up from under water
Moving ships leave a wake: a bow wave of foam at the stem, a foam trail behind the stern and foam along the waterline when fast
Foam quads per tick for every block of stern width at full speed; the bow wave and the waterline foam scale with it
The wake is at its densest and most opaque from this speed in blocks per second on
Life of the stern trail's foam in ticks (the bow wave lives three quarters of it): the longer, the longer the trail
No wake below this speed through the water in blocks per second
Ships within this horizontal distance of the camera in blocks leave a wake
Angle in degrees between the course and each arm of the bow wave's V (19.5 is the Kelvin angle of real ships)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.ampl: Multiplier on the wave height of every sea state (calm 0.15, moderate 0.6, rough 1.2, storm 2.0 blocks); 0 = flat sea
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.boat: Vanilla boats on the open sea rise and fall with the waves (not in lakes, rivers, shallow water or inside a hull)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.comp: Wave trains the sea is made of (16 to 64 blocks long, weighted around the sea state's peak); more gives a less regular rhythm
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.dire: Seconds over which the waves crossfade from the old direction to the new one (0 = switch at once)
The waves turn to a new direction once the wind (with a slow offset) has moved this many degrees away from theirs
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.enab: The sea state follows the weather, rocks ships with roll and pitch and spills water into low open hulls. Off = always a flat sea
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.floa: Items floating on the open sea bob with the waves
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.grou: How much the wave height swells and fades in sets (wave groups): 0.35 = between 65 % and 135 % of the sea state's height
Time scale of the wave groups in seconds: sets of bigger waves come and go over about this long
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.heav: Ships rise on wave crests and sink into troughs (a vertical force from the mean wave height under the hull)
Upper limit of the heave force per kpg of ship mass
Heave force per block of mean wave height under the hull, as a share of the ship's weight
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.max_: Upper limit of the wave torque per kpg of ship mass, so that small boats are not flipped
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.ship: Roll and pitch torque per unit of wave slope and per kpg of ship mass, scaled by (blocks / 200)^-size_exponent
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.size: How much steadier big ships lie: the wave torque per kpg falls as (blocks / 200) to the power of minus this
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.spil: Wave crests spill water over low rims and through low open hatches into compartments
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.stat: Seconds the sea takes to go from calm to storm (or back) when the weather changes
pirates_n_ships.configuration.waves.sync: Ticks between sea state updates sent to players (clients blend between them)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.gust_: Largest change of wind direction during a gust, in degrees
Extra wind strength at the peak of the strongest gust, as a fraction (0.4 = +40%)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.gusts: Thunderstorms produce short gusts of extra wind
Average number of gusts per minute during a full thunderstorm
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.max_s: Highest clear-weather wind speed in blocks per second (raised to min_strength if lower)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.min_s: Lowest clear-weather wind speed in blocks per second
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.regio: Largest regional deviation of the wind direction, in degrees
Distance in blocks over which the regional wind pattern changes
Largest regional deviation of the wind strength, as a fraction (0.3 = plus or minus 30%)
Wind direction and strength differ by region instead of being the same everywhere in a dimension
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.sync_: How often the wind is sent to each player, in ticks
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.varia: How fast wind direction and strength drift. 1 = direction changes over about one in-game day, 0 = frozen
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind.weath: Rain and thunderstorms strengthen the wind and storms bring gusts
pirates_n_ships.configuration.wind_effec: Wind streaks spawned per tick for every block per second of wind speed
Extra streaks at the peak of a gust, as a fraction (1 = twice as many)
Each streak's heading strays up to this many degrees from the wind's
Streaks fly from 1 block up to at most this many blocks above the sea (the top of the rigging)
Most streaks fly this many blocks above the sea (deck height), fewer higher up toward 'height'
Mean life of one streak in ticks, including fading in and out; each lives 0.625 to 1.5 times this
No streaks below this wind speed in blocks per second (calm air)
Opacity of a streak in a strong wind (12 blocks per second and more); at 4 blocks per second it is 0.3 times this
Share of the streaks that come in loose puffs in a steady wind (the rest trickle singly); a gust raises it to all
Most streaks in one puff (a puff has half this, rounded up, to this many)
A puff's streaks start within this many blocks of its centre
A puff's streaks are born over this many ticks
Horizontal distance from the camera in blocks within which streaks appear
Each streak flies at 1 plus or minus this times the wind speed (0.3: 0.7 to 1.3 times)
White wind streaks drift with the wind through the air over the sea, so you can see where the wind blows
Largest gentle up-and-down wobble of a streak over its flight in blocks (each wobbles 0.2 to 1 times this)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.world.spaw: Spawn weight of navy officers at navy outposts (0 = never spawn naturally)
Spawn weight of navy soldiers at navy outposts (0 = never spawn naturally)
Spawn weight of pirates on pirate islands (0 = never spawn naturally)
Spawn weight of sailors in seafarer villages (0 = never spawn naturally)
Spawn weight of sharks in deep ocean biomes, compared to vanilla ocean mobs such as cod (15) and dolphins (2)
pirates_n_ships.configuration.world.stru: Navy outposts generate in new chunks (off = no new outposts; existing ones stay)
Chance that navy outposts generate at a possible location (0 = never, 1 = always); read at placement
Navy officers placed in the fort's court beside the harbor master's office when a new outpost generates (they take turn-ins, fines and ransoms); never despawn or respawn. 0 = none

Navy soldiers placed at their posts (gate, walls, the building) when a new outpost generates; they stand guard and never despawn or respawn. Capped by the posts the outpost's layout has (at least 6). 0 = none
An outpost site farther than this (blocks) from sea water is skipped
An outpost site whose ground at the fort gate is more than this many blocks above sea level is skipped (the gate's paving is laid one block above the sea)
Minimum distance in chunks between two navy outposts. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:navy_outposts; change it with a datapack, not here
How far (blocks) an outpost site looks in each direction for the sea; the direction with the most water gets the quay
Average distance in chunks between two navy outposts. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:navy_outposts; change it with a datapack, not here
The treasure spot of a new camp gets a buried chest (loot table pirates_n_ships:chests/buried_treasure), recorded on the port as a treasure site; off = the marker stays plain sand
Pirate island camps generate in new chunks (off = no new camps; existing ones stay)
Chance that pirate islands generate at a possible location (0 = never, 1 = always); read at placement
A camp site farther than this (blocks) from sea water is skipped
Pirates stop spawning naturally in a camp once this many pirates are within 32 blocks of the spawn spot
A camp site whose ground at the camp is more than this many blocks above sea level is skipped (the camp's sand is laid one block above the sea)
Minimum distance in chunks between two pirate islands. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:pirate_islands; change it with a datapack, not here
How far (blocks) a camp site looks in each direction for the sea; the direction with the most water gets the jetty
Average distance in chunks between two pirate islands. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:pirate_islands; change it with a datapack, not here
Seafarer villages generate in new chunks (off = no new villages; existing ones stay)
Chance that seafarer villages generate at a possible location (0 = never, 1 = always); read at placement
A village site farther than this (blocks) from sea water is skipped
A village site whose ground at the dock head is more than this many blocks above sea level is skipped (the quay is built one block above the sea)
Minimum distance in chunks between two seafarer villages. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:seafarer_villages; change it with a datapack, not here
How far (blocks) a village site looks in each direction for the sea; the direction with the most water gets the pier
Average distance in chunks between two seafarer villages. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:seafarer_villages; change it with a datapack, not here
Wrecks generate on the ocean floor of new chunks (off = no new wrecks; existing ones stay)
Chance that wrecks generate at a possible location (0 = never, 1 = always); read at placement
Minimum distance in chunks between two wrecks. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:wrecks; change it with a datapack, not here
Average distance in chunks between two wrecks. Datapack value: this default is written into the structure set pirates_n_ships:wrecks; change it with a datapack, not here
pirates_n_ships.configuration.world.trea: Blank treasure maps bind to a treasure when used and fences sell them (off = blank maps stay blank, fences stop selling them; bound maps keep their picture)
How far (blocks, to the island's centre) a blank map looks for a pirate island with an unfound treasure
pirates_n_ships.configuration.world_simu: Tell a hunted ship's owner when a captain gives chase or breaks off
Blocks within which the captain counts as in contact with his quarry (resets the give-up timer)
Ticks between two course updates of a captain's ship chasing its quarry (and between calls to man the guns)
A captain's chase course is only given anew when the quarry moved at least this many blocks since the last one
A captain sails this many blocks out (along the lane toward a village or outpost within this distance, else into open sea) and back to his island
Pirate captains put to sea. Off = no new voyages; a captain at sea sails home and hunts nobody
A captain who has not come within contact_distance of his quarry for this many ticks breaks off the chase
A captain hunts the ship of a player who holds a letter of marque
A captain hunts the ship of a player carrying at least this many bounty proofs (0 = proofs never draw him)
A captain at sea sights a hunted player's ship within this many blocks (0 = he hunts nobody)
A quarry farther than this many blocks from the captain is lost, and he returns to his course
Distance in blocks the captain's ship keeps from its quarry: it circles it at this range with its guns firing
Ticks the captain's ship lies by a quarry that struck its colours, guns silent, before it sails on
Chance that a captain puts to sea when his day comes (every voyage_days days)
Days between two chances of a captain at his post to put to sea
Average number of trade convoys that set out per in-game day across the world
Simulate NPC ships travelling between ports, faction tension and pirate raids. Off = no NPC voyages or raids
How far aggression (toward 0.3) and tension (toward 0) move back each in-game day
Strength of the players' deeds (plunder, kills, turn-ins) on the faction state. 0 = ignored
Keep a faction state that deeds and world events shift and that decays every day. Off = the state stays as it is
Strength of world events (NPC kills, convoys, raids, lost patrols) on the faction state. 0 = ignored
Most wealth (abstract doubloons) a faction can hold
Contract risk of a lane with no pirate island near it
Side of one sea grid cell in blocks (smaller = finer lanes, slower to find)
Lane search budget per grid cell of straight distance between the ports (between min_cells and max_cells; 0 = always max_cells)
Lanes may cross beach cells of the biome map (often shallow water off a coast, and a port's bay can be ringed by them) at shore_cost; off = only ocean biomes are sea
How far (in cells) from a port's berth the lane may start when the berth's own cell is not sea
Cost multiplier for sea cells next to land, so lanes keep off the coasts (1 = hug the coast)
Most grid cells one lane search may expand, however far apart the ports are
Server time in milliseconds a background lane search may use per voyage check; a longer search continues in the next check
Grid cells every lane search may expand, however close the ports are
Ticks before a port pair without a lane is searched again (24000 = one day)
Contract risk added by each pirate island near the lane (combined as 1 - (1 - r)^n)
Pirate islands within this many blocks of a lane make delivery contracts on it riskier (and pay more)
Cost multiplier for crossing a beach cell, so lanes use them only to leave a bay or pass a strait
Raise to throw away every cached lane (e.g. after changing the grid settings)
Rounds (one gunpowder and one cannonball each) per cannon put in the shot locker of a navy or pirate ship when it appears (0 = none; merchants carry none)
Ticks a player must stay aboard an NPC ship whose fighters are all dead to capture it
Goods aboard an NPC ship carry the plunder mark, so whatever a player takes from it sells as plunder
Chain shot (with one gunpowder each) put in every stocked shot locker of a navy or pirate ship when it appears (0 = none)
Deckhands on an NPC ship besides its helmsman (they work the sails through the job board)
Turn NPC voyages near players into real ships. Off = voyages stay abstract records (ships already at sea stay)
Armed sailors guarding a merchant ship
Navy soldiers on a navy ship (the first is an officer)
Grapeshot (with one gunpowder each) put in every stocked shot locker of a navy or pirate ship when it appears (0 = none)
The cannons of a navy or pirate ship appear loaded, so its first shot needs no reload
Blocks beyond materialize_radius within which a player still keeps an NPC ship real
Ticks an NPC ship stays real after the last player left its surroundings (materialize_radius + linger_margin)

One of an NPC ship's deckhands keeps watch in its crow's nest (if it has one), so the nest counts as manned (a navy observer's wider false-colours watch). Off = nobody goes up; the deckhand works the sails
Most NPC voyages that are real ships at the same time in the whole world
A ship that appears again is flooded back to the health its voyage kept (1 - flooded part when it last turned into a record), lowest compartments first. Off = it always appears dry
Ticks before a voyage that could not appear (land, no water, obstructed) or got stuck is tried again
Ticks a player's cannon hit still counts as the cause when the ship sinks
Ticks the whole ship must stay under the sea surface to count as sunk
Part of the hull's inside volume under water at which an NPC ship counts as sunk
Ticks the chunks at a voyage's spawn point are kept loaded while it waits to appear
Distance in blocks from a player at which an NPC voyage becomes a real ship with crew
Most NPC voyages (convoys and patrols) that can exist at the same time in the whole world
Tell a hunted ship's owner when a patrol gives chase, breaks off, or accepts the surrender
Blocks within which a patrol counts as in contact with its quarry (resets the give-up timer)
Ticks between two course updates of a patrol ship chasing its quarry
A patrol ship's course is only given anew when its quarry moved at least this many blocks since the last one
Navy patrols set out and hunt. Off = no new patrols, and patrols at sea stop hunting and sail their route
A patrol that has not come within contact_distance of its quarry for this many ticks breaks off the chase

Doubloons of bounty on a ship's owner from which the navy hunts the ship whatever flag it flies (a ship is also hunted under the Jolly Roger, with its cover blown, or with its owner wanted at law.world.navy_hostility_threshold)
A patrol sights a player's ship within this many blocks (horizontally) and gives chase if it is hunted
A quarry farther than this many blocks from the patrol is lost, and the patrol returns to its route
A patrol sails to another navy outpost at most this far away (blocks between centres); else it sails out and back
A lone outpost's patrol sails this many blocks out along the lane toward the nearest pirate island and back
Distance in blocks a patrol keeps from its quarry: it circles it at this range
Ticks a patrol shadows a ship that struck its colours, guns silent, before it returns to its route
Average number of navy patrols that set out per in-game day across the world
Tell the players at the settlement when raiders are sighted and how the raid ended
Blocks out at sea from the settlement's berth at which the raiders appear
Ticks the settlement's bells ring (every 100 ticks) after a raid is sighted (0 = no bells)
Highest raid chance per minute the growth can reach (0 = no raids)
How much the raid chance per minute rises for every minute (1200 ticks) a player spends at a navy settlement
In-game days after a raid before the same settlement can be raided again
Pirates raid navy settlements while players stay there. Off = no raids start (raids under way go on)
Within this many blocks of the berth the raiders anchor and their fighters go ashore
Ticks the raiders fight ashore before the survivors go back and the ships withdraw
With retaliation_enabled the raid chance growth is multiplied by 1 + this x the Navy-Pirates tension (0..1)
Pirate ships that sail in one raid
Seafarer villages are raided too, not only navy outposts
High tension between factions makes them raid each other's settlements and convoys more often
Units of each good a convoy buys at its origin and sells at its destination
Ports farther apart than this (blocks between centres) never send convoys to each other
Ports closer than this (blocks between centres) never send convoys to each other
Speed factor with the wind straight astern
Speed factor with the wind straight ahead (beam reach is halfway between)
Ship templates merchant convoys sail (one is picked at random)
Ship templates navy patrols sail (one is picked at random)
Ship templates pirate raiders sail (one is picked at random)
Speed of an abstract voyage in blocks per second, before the wind factor
Ticks between two voyage updates (movement, arrivals, spawn rolls)
Voyages sail faster downwind and slower into the wind
