pirates_n_ships.jei.market.produced: Where it is made: buy for %s
pirates_n_ships.jei.market.produced_nowh: Made only by some kinds of port
pirates_n_ships.jei.provisions.spoils: Spoils after %s days in the pantry
pirates_n_ships.market.status.plunder_re: The harbor master wants no stolen goods
pirates_n_ships.market.status.reputation: The villagers won't trade with you: your reputation with them is too low
pirates_n_ships.market.status.stock_limi: Over the port's stock or demand
pirates_n_ships.ponder.ratline_nets.head: Ratline Nets
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.anchor_and: The capstan works the anchor. It hangs outside the hull just below the deck, on the side nearer the capstan
A crew member at the capstan works it on the whistle's Drop anchor and Weigh anchor
Over water deeper than the chain is long (32 blocks) the capstan refuses to let go: no ground to hold
Pulling harder than it holds drags the anchor over the seabed; if the chain runs out first, it does not hold at all
Use the capstan to let go: the anchor falls by its own weight and the chain runs out after it
Once it bites, the chain pulls her up softly, never to a dead stop, and she swings to lie head to her chain
It sinks about 4 blocks a second and lands on the seabed; with way on, she leaves it a few blocks astern
Use the capstan again to weigh anchor: the chain comes in at 2.5 blocks a second
Anchor up and stowed: she is free to sail
While he works, the bars turn and he walks round the drum pushing them
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.b: Or blow Board! on the whistle: your hands cross the plank or a two-block gap and fight; Back aboard calls them home
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.c: Your boarders fence by the same rules; a hand with an empty fist takes a sword from your chests
Cross over: the plank is a thin board you walk on like a deck
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.f: Her crew fights with the same swordplay as you: watch the raised arm, parry just before the blow, riposte
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.h: While you stand on your deck holding the line, it hauls both hulls together until they lie alongside
Throw your grappling hook, or shoot it from a musket, onto the other ship: it bites into her hull
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.l: It lies rail top to rail top. Three wooden slabs over two iron nuggets make one
Taking a merchant is piracy; a pirate ship taken under a letter of marque pays prize money
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.boarding.p: When the hulls drift more than 1.5 blocks apart, the plank breaks and drops
Use a boarding plank on the top of your gunwale: one straight board, up to 6 blocks, onto her deck
A ship of the seas is yours once none of her fighters is left and you have stood aboard for 5 seconds
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.cannon_loa: Sneak and use the upper half of the gun to raise the barrel, the lower half to lower it
Then use a cannonball on it (chain shot and grapeshot load the same way)
Use the cannon with an empty hand to fire
The cannon is two blocks long: the muzzle points out through the gun port, the carriage sits behind it
Load it in order: powder first, then the shot, rammed home, then fire
Use gunpowder on the cannon to put the powder in
The rammer seats the charge as you load: once the shot is in, the gun is ready
The recoil pushes your ship back, and the barrel needs a moment before it can be loaded again
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.cargo_and_: Stowed aft, the load trims her by the stern, and she sits lower in the water
Every ship is ballasted when she is assembled, so that she floats level with her holds empty
Cargo crates, cargo barrels, pantries and water barrels grow heavier as they fill
A full crate weighs as much as some forty planks
Restowed amidships she floats level again, only deeper
The ship screen at the helm reads her load: Light, Laden, Heavily laden or Overloaded
Her ballast does not count the cargo: trim her yourself, with heavy loads low and amidships
Laden, she gathers way and turns more slowly, and with less freeboard a breach floods her sooner
Placed empty, the crates leave her level: her ballast is worked out again for new blocks
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.crew_order: Lie moored at the port first: the new hand comes straight aboard. Every hand needs a free hammock
Use the whistle on a hand, then on a station: he walks there and takes it until you release him
Fire at will: gun crews aim and fire by themselves at hostile ships within 15° of the barrel and 64 blocks
Hands are hired at a harbor master's desk: its Crew tab offers a few each day, for a fee and then a daily wage
Unmanned stations that take the order become open jobs: a free hand on deck takes the nearest one by himself
An order goes to every hand at a station that takes it: 'Aye, hoisting the sails!'
Release crew sends every hand off his station, drops the open jobs and ends fire at will
The ship screen at the helm (sneak and use it) gives the same orders and shows every hand's morale
Use the captain's whistle in the air, standing on your ship: the order wheel opens. Point at an order and click
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.crows_nest: 'Sail two points to starboard, 140 blocks' over the hotbar, a bell from the nest, a mark on the compass
The crow's nest stands on top of a mast: a log, a fence, a wall or any block with a solid top
A flagpole may stand in the nest: the flag flies above it, and the nest still keeps the lookout
Use the whistle on a hand, then on the nest: he takes his post up there and keeps watch
Ratlines lead up to it: sloped nets from the deck, then nets hung on the mast like a ladder
Only its floor is solid: climb up and step in over the rim, sneaking to stay put
Every 3 seconds the lookout scans 160 blocks round the ship and calls what is new to everyone aboard
Stand in the nest yourself and you keep the lookout
He calls ships by their flags, land, sharks and the kraken; again when they close in, or after 2 minutes
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.flags_and_: Any banner flies as a custom flag with its colours and patterns, and counts as neutral
Caught under false colours, you are charged heavily and the navy hunts your ship for five minutes
The highest flag on her poles is the flag she flies: no flag or a merchant flag is neutral to all
A navy flag lets you pass the navy, unless you are a suspect or worse: then navy watchers may see through it
Use the pole with a flag: in 3 seconds it runs up and flies, and the old one comes back to you
Under the Jolly Roger pirates leave you be, but the navy attacks on sight, and being seen is a crime
A navy ship with a manned crow's nest sees your flag half again as far and half again as fast
A flag pedestal carved from a log seats the pole on any deck, and you can work the flag from it
A flagpole flies your colours. Stack up to 6 for a tall pole: the flag always flies at the top
Use the pole with an empty hand to strike your colours: you surrender, and navy and pirates stop attacking
Firing on a ship that has struck, or on one under a merchant flag or a banner, is a crime
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.galley_and: Every dawn each hand eats a loaf and a bit and drinks one ration from the stores aboard
At noon and at sunset the free hands sit down by the pantry for a few seconds: the meal is only a sight
The pantry is the ship's food store: anything edible counts, by its nourishment
A ration of rum cheers them; more than the ration slows them down for a while
After 8 days without fresh food comes scurvy: weakness and lost morale. A lime, any fruit or fresh food cures it
Hungry hands lose morale and work at 75% speed; thirsty ones lose it faster and work at half speed
Fresh food spoils after 5 days in the pantry; hardtack, salted fish, salt pork and bread keep
A water barrel holds 16 rations of fresh water: a water bucket adds 3, a bottle 1
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.hammocks_a: Each hammock is a bunk: a ship takes on as many hands as she has hammocks
The sea cot is a bed for you, ashore or on an assembled ship; the crew sleep only in hammocks
At dawn he gets up: a night in a hammock gives 5 morale, a night aboard without one costs 10
Hands at a station stay on duty all night, and an order at night gets sleepers up at once
Hang a hammock between two supports at the same height: fence posts, walls, logs or the hull's side
At nightfall every hand not at a station turns in to the nearest free hammock
You sleep in a hammock too, ashore or aboard, and you wake and respawn beside it
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.hull_repai: Stand inside, look at the edge of the hole (the face of a hull block beside it) and use the patch
A breach lets the sea in until it is closed
A tarred plank fills the hole and the inflow stops at once: there is no repair time to wait out
A patch only goes into a real hole in an assembled ship; anywhere else it says so and is not used up
Two planks and a coal or charcoal make two hull patches
Any watertight block in the hole closes it too. Swapping the patch for a plank later opens the hole while you swap
The water already inside stays until it is pumped out
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.al: Bring her in alongside the quay
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.as: From the quay it works the other way round: hook the ship and tie off at the quay's ring. A hook caught on a ring holds twice as far
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.ca: To cast off, sneak and use with an empty hand: the line lets go and the hook comes back
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.cl: Cleats hold a line as rings do, and sliding along a rope needs it tied off on one of them
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.ho: The tied line holds her to the quay, and if she drifts off it hauls her back toward the hook
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.po: Lying within 32 blocks of a port she counts as moored there: hired hands walk straight aboard
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.ri: To hold her alongside, use the grappling hook with a mooring ring (four iron ingots make two) or a cleat
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.th: From the deck, throw your grappling hook onto the quay: the hook bites into the stone
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.mooring.ti: Use the mooring ring on your own ship: the line is tied off there and you can let go
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.bench: An oar bench at the rail is a station: a hand seated on it pulls a quarter harder than one standing
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.faste: The hands ship the oars by themselves once the sails drive the ship faster than the oars can
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.push: Each oar pushes along the bow, in a calm or against the wind, up to 3 blocks a second; sails add to it
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.rail: Without a bench a hand rows standing at the rail, the sides taken in turn so the ship runs straight
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.row: Row on the whistle: every hand who is not at a station takes an oar. No block is needed
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.oars.ship: Use the same entry again, now Ship oars, or give any other order: the oars come in and the hands go back
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.al: It hangs along the rail as a boarding net
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.ba: The same entry, now Back aboard, calls them home
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.ca: Any order calls him off at once
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.cu: Three cutlass blows cut a boarding net down
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.he: A boarder coming over the rail is held a moment
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.id: A hand with nothing to do may lean on the railing a while
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.lo: He watches the sea, turning his head now and then
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.ne: String a ratline net between two chainplates on top of one railing
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.ov: Then he may climb over: have your blades ready
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.on_deck.pa: Your own crew pass it freely: Board! on the whistle sends them over
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.pumps_and_: A hull block destroyed below the waterline is a breach: the sea runs into the room behind it
A crew member at the pump works it on the whistle's Man the pumps until the bilge is dry
Now the pump wins, and the water goes down until the bilge is dry
While the hull is whole, the hold below the waterline stays dry
Against an open breach one pump only holds the level: close the hole
Use a hull patch on the edge of the hole: the inflow stops at once
Hold use on a bilge pump to pump about a block of water a second from the highest flooded room below it
The bigger and deeper the hole, the faster it comes: a 1×1 hole one block down lets in about a block a second
Its pipe reaches 4 blocks down through the planks, so it may stand on the hold floor or on the deck above
Flood water weighs her down. Rooms joined by an open door or hatch level out; a closed door holds it back
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.b: A bulwark is a solid wall: a gun behind it fires into it
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.c: Click a railing again to rail a second edge: a corner
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.f: A cannon behind the port fires through it at any elevation
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.g: A railing gate swings open like a fence gate
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.l: A lantern stands on a railing post or hangs under it
Cut a gun port: its lid opens when a cannon stands behind it
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.p: Open, it takes a gangway: lay a boarding plank from its sill
A railing port leaves a one-block opening
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.r: A railing sits on the edge of its block. Posts stand where a run ends
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.railings.s: A swivel gun mounts on the rail, out on its edge
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.ratline_ne: Break a chainplate and its strand falls; break the hoop and all do
Walk into the net and hold forward to climb; sneak to hold on
Up to five chainplates can share one hoop
Neighbouring strands fan into one net: climb anywhere on it
A chainplate on the rail, a mast hoop on the mast
The line must be clear, 30° steep or more and at most 32 blocks
Use a ratline net on one fitting, then on the other
Climb on past the hoop and walk forward to step off
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.sails_and_: The cloth is drawn between the yards, not built from blocks: its area is the mean yard length times the drop, 5 × 4 = 20 here
A crew member at the winch hoists, reefs and furls on the captain's whistle
Use it again: full sail, down to the lower yard. A third time furls it again
Furled, the cloth is a roll under the upper yard and gives no force
Use the winch once: half sail, the cloth hangs half way down
A square sail hangs between two yards on a mast of logs or fences
A second yard of the same direction 2 to 8 blocks straight below the first makes the pair one sail
When the wind freshens, reef to half sail (from full the winch goes round furled, then half): less cloth, less force, less heel
The sail winch sets the trim of every sail on its ship
The wind fills the cloth and it bellies out to leeward. Square sails like the wind from astern; within 30° of the wind no sail drives
Using an upper yard with an empty hand trims that one sail only
A yard is a straight row of yard blocks across the ship. It hangs one block forward of the mast, its middle block in the column in front of it
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.ship_assem: Blocks placed on her afterwards become part of her at once
Now she is one ship: she floats, rolls with the sea and keeps her hold dry
Build your ship from any blocks, right on the water: this hull keeps a dry hold below the waterline
To take her apart, sneak and use the helm with an empty hand and press Disassemble on the ship screen twice
Everything that touches the hull becomes part of the ship, so leave a gap of water to the shore or a dock
Place a helm on deck. Its helmsman stands behind it, and the way he looks is the bow
She must lie nearly still and level: her heading is rounded to the nearest quarter turn and her blocks are set back into the world
Air, water and terrain such as sand, dirt and stone are never taken along
Use the helm: every block connected to it, up to 2048, becomes one ship
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.ship_ident: A name board fixed on her side shows her name
A figurehead hangs on the bow block you click and looks toward you
Name her at the helm: use a named name tag on it once she is launched
A captain with a rank puts his title in front when he names her
The longer the row, the larger the letters and the farther they read
Any sign and a gold nugget make three name boards
Boards side by side join: the name grows across the row
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.ships_bell: In a navy outpost every bell rings the alarm when pirates come to raid it
Nothing else is tied to it: no watch, no order, and your crew does not ring it. It is your signal
Hang the ship's bell on a wall, or stand it in its frame on a post or any block with a firm middle
Three sticks over three gold ingots and an iron nugget make one
Use it to ring it: the bell swings away from you and rings out
Struck from the side, it rocks at half the swing
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.c: Hard over she turns on a circle three to four ship lengths across, at any speed: slower only takes longer
The whistle and the ship screen give no course yet, only a server operator can: he then steers for each mark in turn
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.h: A crew member can hold a course: use the captain's whistle on him, then on the helm
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.l: Let go and the wheel stays where you left it; the line above the hotbar shows the rudder angle
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.r: The rudder follows the wheel, up to 35° each way at three quarters of a turn
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.t: Take the wheel yourself at any time and he lets go; release it and he steers on
Move the mouse or hold A and D to turn it: right turns her to starboard, left to port
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.steering.w: The rudder only bites while she moves through the water, and it works the other way when she goes astern
On an assembled ship, hold use on the helm to take the wheel
pirates_n_ships.ponder.shared.swivel_gun: Hold use with an empty hand: it turns wherever you look, all round, from 30° down to 45° up
Chain shot and grapeshot are for the cannon only: the swivel takes a cannonball
A hand at the swivel fires it on the whistle's Fire!, and loads it on Load! from powder and shot nearby
The swivel gun mounts on a fence, a wall, iron bars, brig bars or any block with a solid top
Load it like the cannon: gunpowder first
It hits less hard and less far than the cannon, breaks no planks, and cools for 3 seconds before new powder
